stimuli.description: Two distinct light settings in a climate chamber: 'warm, dim light' (CCT 2708 K, 97 lux) and 'cool, bright light' (CCT 5854 K, 1021 lux).

tables.description: Participant descriptors including Body Mass Index, Midsleep (MSFsc), PSQI score, General Health (SF-36), and Light Sensitivity (Eye Problems, Headache, Sunglasses) and Thermal Sensitivity.
a-opic irradiances of the light settings (S-cone-opic, M-cone-opic, L-cone-opic, Rhodopic, Melanopic) for Warm, dim light and Cool, bright light.
key_stats: Irradiance values in lux for different photoreceptors

tables.description: Test statistics (t-ratio and p-value) of the main effect of light transition (WD to CB vs. Constant WD, and CB to WD vs. Constant CB) on various dependent variables.

limitations: CCT and illuminance were manipulated simultaneously, preventing attribution of effects to either factor.
Time of day effects on light responsiveness could not be tested due to group sizes.
Abrupt transitions were used, and more gradual transitions might yield different results.
Generalizability limited by laboratory setting and specific cultural background of participants.
Study duration was only 90 min, requiring validation in longer experiments and field settings.
